check_text:
protocol.py: 2 biology problems (2 warnings).

1. WARNING COLD-MODULE-NEVER-SET: A temperature module was loaded but never set
   line 44:  p20.aspirate(2, block["A1"])
   At line 44 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 7 more in slot
   1, on a temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at
   room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), enzyme
   (reagent), plasmid 1 (sample), plasmid 10 (sample) and 11 more sat on a block that was
   never cold; the robot pipetted there 48 times over the run. The person setting up the
   deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2
   and 7 more in slot 1.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 7 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24
   Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 1, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at
   the end.
   Source: Opentrons, temperature module: at room temperature until set_temperature, which
   blocks
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/temperature_module.html
   Source: Thermo Fisher T4 ligase manual: keep on ice, use within minutes
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/t4dnaligase_1U_man.pdf
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   [61a9a24a7061]

2. WARNING ENZYME-BEFORE-DILUENT: An enzyme was added before the water: enzyme
   line 51:  p20.dispense(1, plate[f"A{i}"])
   At line 51 the robot put enzyme into wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in
   slot 2 (this line did it 12 times). Take well A1 in slot 2: at that moment it held only 2
   ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at line 63, to make the 14 ul
   of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is
   meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought
   the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many
   times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star
   activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Reorder the additions to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 2:
   water and buffer first, then the sample, then enzyme last. Or make a master mix of water,
   buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.
   Source: Thermo Fisher: restriction enzyme key considerations (the enzyme is the final
   component)
           https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cloning/cloning-learning-center/invitrogen-school-of-molecular-biology/molecular-cloning/restriction-enzymes/restriction-enzyme-key-considerations.html
   Source: Promega: restriction enzyme resource (add the enzyme last; glycerol and star
   activity)
           https://www.promega.com/resources/guides/nucleic-acid-analysis/restriction-enzyme-resource/
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   Source: Qiagen: critical factors for successful real-time PCR (order of addition)
           https://www.gene-quantification.de/qiagen-qpcr-sample-assay-tech-guide-2010.pdf
   [2803879ba210]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: A temperature module was loaded but never set
findings.explanation: At line 44 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 7 more in slot 1, on a temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), enzyme (reagent), plasmid 1 (sample), plasmid 10 (sample) and 11 more sat on a block that was never cold; the robot pipetted there 48 times over the run. The person setting up the deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 7 more in slot 1.
findings.fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24 Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 1, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at the end.

findings.title: An enzyme was added before the water: enzyme
findings.explanation: At line 51 the robot put enzyme into wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 2 (this line did it 12 times). Take well A1 in slot 2: at that moment it held only 2 ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at line 63, to make the 14 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
findings.fix: Reorder the additions to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 2: water and buffer first, then the sample, then enzyme last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.
